result.title: When to Intervene? An Empirical Study of Errors and Self-Recovery in LLM Agents
result.summary: LLM agents interact with Web services to perform tasks on users' behalf. Errors during these interactions can disrupt execution and prevent task completion, motivating external intervention. However, agents may self-recover through continued execution, raising the question of when to intervene and when to wait for self-recovery. We present an empirical study of errors and self-recovery in LLM agents. We construct ReInBench, a dataset containing 1,259 agent traces and 1,403 error events across computer-use and Web tasks. Our study examines how often and how quickly agents self-recover, how self-recovery relates to subsequent execution and task completion, and whether self-recovery can be predicted when an error occurs. We find that 725 error events self-recover, often within a few steps, with self-recovery performance differing across Execution LLMs. Self-recovery can also help agents recover from subsequent errors of the same type and support overall task completion. Intervention should therefore prioritize errors unlikely to self-recover, while allowing agents to continue when self-recovery is likely. Building on these empirical findings, we propose ReCoF, a method that predicts whether an error will self-recover to inform whether additional intervention is needed. ReCoF achieves an average relative improvement of 9.02% in Macro-F1 over the strongest baseline on ReInBench. Our code and data can be found at https://method-notes.github.io/ReCoF/.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建 ReInBench（1,259 条 agent 轨迹、1,403 个错误事件），实证分析 LLM agent 在 Web 与 computer-use 任务中错误自恢复的频率、速度及其与任务完成的关系，并提出 ReCoF 预测某错误是否会被自恢复，以决定是否外部干预。
AI.relevance_reason: 「何时干预、何时等待自恢复」与 LVR 中 STOP 的收益-成本权衡可作概念类比，可供核查 ReCoF 式的继续/停止预测思路能否迁移到 latent 推理的停止判别；论文本身不涉及视觉表征或 latent 生成。
